title: Does calculated MCHC add transportable inflammation prediction beyond its components? An exploratory two-survey test
abstract: We tested calculated mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC=100*Hb/Hct) for incremental prediction of concurrent CRP>3mg/L beyond separate nonlinear Hb/Hct, MCV, RDW and routine covariates. Models fitted in 14,401 NHANES III adults were transported without recalibration to 4,596 separately recruited NHANES2017–2018 adults. Weighted Brier changed from 0.17436607 to 0.17427645; added-minus-base -0.00008962, approximate fixed-fit target-PSU95% interval [-0.00031823,+0.00015420]. AUC delta was +0.00045595; joint training/target Brier interval [-0.00033008,+0.00016854]. This is an exploratory representation test in historically reused cohorts, not a new biomarker, causal study or clinical validation. The primary uncertainty criterion does not establish an incremental predictive advantage.
